O01-3 used high-resolution manometry before and two hours after oral levodopa in three men with stage 5 Parkinson dysphagia. Pharyngeal contractile integral increased in two and fell in one. Upper esophageal sphincter relaxation pressure improved clearly in one. No food or test bolus was named. Adjacent O01-4 used 3 g of unspecified jelly in a swallowing-endoscopy method validation without a reported Parkinson subgroup.

O03-4 studied 11 suspected idiopathic noninflammatory cricopharyngeal myopathy cases. Parkinson progression was among background conditions initially considered explanations for sudden worsening. No Parkinson subgroup count, food, or food effect. The adjacent thickened water and water jelly case O03-3 involved myasthenia gravis.

O13-3 compared tongue-elevation muscle activity in 22 Parkinson patients and 14 healthy controls and described changes after cervical electrical stimulation. No food bolus or food-specific outcome. Adjacent O13-4 used cup-sipped barium and a mock tablet in a separate 30-person swallowing analysis without a reported Parkinson subgroup.

P3-3 describes a man with Parkinson disease and diabetes who ate an unnamed regular diet at home after subglottic laryngeal closure. He continued oral and gastrostomy feeding after later pneumonia and experienced three further pneumonias. Videofluoroscopy found no closure-site leak, and the authors suspected a nonaspiration mechanism. No ingredient or meal-level association is given.
